definition: Upward communication is open communication in which staff share ideas or speak up within an organizational hierarchy, helping leaders create a more inclusive and psychologically safe environment. In this context, it supports innovation by making it easier for nurses to express and implement new ideas.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define “upward communication” as “open communication in which staff share ideas or speak up within an organizational hierarchy.”
Because that description of the mechanism/scope of upward communication is not stated in the packet, the definition’s first sentence contains unsupported substantive claims.

The remaining elements that *are* supported (encouraging upward communication to create an inclusive, psychologically safe environment and empower nurses to generate and implement innovative ideas) are part of the definition, but the definition as a whole is not fully supported.

The packet does not define upward communication as open communication in which staff share ideas or speak up within an organizational hierarchy; it only says responsible leadership can encourage upward communication.
The definition adds a broader generic meaning and organizational detail that are not stated in the source packet.
The field assignment is not well supported by the packet, which frames the term in organizational/leadership and innovation terms rather than ethics specifically.
